title: Add RAG agent templates and tool-calling examples; update docs site
author: Ava Thompson
release_notes: Added RAG agent templates, tool-calling example apps, and docs site quickstarts. No breaking API changes. See examples and docs for migration notes.
body: Context: This PR adds a set of RAG agent templates and end-to-end tool-calling example apps to the redwood-examples repo and updates the docs site with quickstart pages and new diagrams. Motivation: Provide engineers with production-ready starting points for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) + agent/tool-calling flows that demonstrate best-practices for prompt design, memory/KV cache considerations, and safe tool integration. What this includes: - three agent templates (question-answering agent, synthesis/summary agent, and multi-tool orchestration agent) under redwood-examples/rag/templates - two full example apps that demonstrate HTTP tool-calling and search integration under redwood-examples/agents/tool-calling - docs site pages and quickstart walk-throughs under redwood-docs/docs/rag and docs/quickstarts/tool-calling - small runtime compatibility shim to expose structured tool-call metadata from the SDK (backwards compatible) Checklist: - [x] Add agent templates and README with usage examples - [x] Add tool-calling example apps with docker-compose and tests - [x] Update docs site quickstarts and API reference - [x] Add unit + integration tests for examples - [x] CI green and manual spot-checks on staging Notes on implementation: - Templates are parameterized and include recommended cache/prefix settings to match typical production traffic patterns (small batch sizes, prefix caching for conversational flows). - The tool-calling examples use a lightweight local tool harness (HTTP echo + external search stub) and include instructions for swapping in a real search backend. - The SDK shim is intentionally minimal: it returns a structured tool_call event on the response envelope; existing code paths that don't inspect tool_call remain unchanged. Migration: Users can adopt the templates without code changes; the SDK shim is backwards compatible. For teams relying on custom tool parsers, see the docs page for a sample adapter. Testing and CI: - Unit tests added for template generation and parsing logic - Integration tests run the example apps in CI with the tool harness - Docs site build step updated to include the new pages Rollout plan: Merge to main, publish examples package, then trigger docs site deploy. Follow up: monitor telemetry for any increase in errors from tool-call parsing and add additional e2e tests if needed.

notes: Manual staging smoke tested the two example apps. Observability: added a lightweight telemetry flag to examples to opt into sending anonymized usage for initial monitoring.
changelog_entry: Added RAG agent templates and tool-calling examples, plus docs quickstarts and SDK shim for structured tool_call events.
